title: The 10% Early-Withdrawal Penalty (and the 5 Exceptions)
subtitle: Pull earnings from your Roth before 59½ and the IRS takes ten percent. But there are five exceptions that erase the penalty.
source_irs: IRC §72(t); IRS Topic No. 557 — Additional Tax on Early Distributions

concepts.heading: The 10% Penalty
concepts.lede: Take your gains out before 59½ — there's a 10% tax on the earnings, on top of regular income tax.
body: Earnings pulled early = 10% penalty + ordinary income tax.
Contributions can come out anytime, tax- and penalty-free. You already paid tax on them.
The penalty applies to the EARNINGS only, not the principal.

concepts.heading: The 5 Exceptions
concepts.lede: Five IRS-recognized exceptions waive the 10% penalty, even before 59½.
body: 1. First-time home purchase — up to $10,000 lifetime.
5. Birth or adoption expense — up to $5,000 per child.

concepts.heading: The Strategy
concepts.lede: Max the Roth. The 5 exceptions cover most emergencies. The penalty is a guardrail, not a trap.
body: Stack 6-12 months of expenses in a brokerage for true emergencies.
Keep the Roth untouched until 59½ (and the 5-year rule).
The 10% penalty is what makes the Roth's tax-free growth possible.
